turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels, process/composition
    columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B, Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment
    step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2
    temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3
    temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3 cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2 temperature, Secondary treatment step 2
    time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3 time, Secondary treatment step 4
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure temperature, Thermal exposure time) and
    the two measured objectives `yield strength (MPa)` and `elongation (%)`
    (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose objectives were
    NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same process/composition
    columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH elongation (%). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), elongation (%)) plane, so a set of
mutually non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates
that are all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning

**1. Learn the frontier from training data.** The training Pareto front in (YS, elongation) is roughly:
- ~206–290 MPa @ 60–80% (solution-annealed austenitics, e.g. 18Cr/9Ni at 1050–1100 °C)
- ~310–375 MPa @ 50–55% (e.g. 20.5Cr/13.5Ni/2.5Si @ 1150 °C → 375/53)
- ~600–1000 MPa @ 22–34% (Ti-rich γ′ alloys, 11.25Cr/19.5–23Ni/2.9Ti aged ~700–735 °C → 700/34, 1000/25)
- ~1300–1580 MPa @ 10–16% (martensitic 11–13Cr steels tempered at 400–475 °C → 1330–1380/13–15)

**2. Match pool candidates to near-identical training rows.**

- **c018** (18Cr/8.75Ni/0.4Ti, 1050 °C + 700 °C/20h temper): identical training route without aging gave **278 MPa / 62%**; aging at 600 °C barely changed similar alloys → ~280/58. Best elongation anchor available.
- **c051** (20.5Cr/13.5Ni/2.5Si, 1100 °C/0.5h): training twin (1150 °C) gave **375 MPa / 53%** — strong high-ductility point that likely dominates other austenitic options.
- **c012** (11.25Cr/19.5Ni/2.9Ti, aged 750 °C/16h): training twin (1050 °C + 700 °C/3h) gave **700 MPa / 34%**; similar 2.9Ti alloys aged 725 °C/16h gave 600/25 → ~650–700/28–32. Excellent knee point.
- **c056** (11.25Cr/23Ni/2.9Ti/1.3Mo, aged 735 °C/16h): the same alloy fully aged (720 °C/16h + 640 °C/13h) gave **1000 MPa / 25%** → expect ~850–950/22. Second knee, filling the mid-high strength gap.
- **c053** (11.25Cr/1.65Ni/1.8W martensitic, tempered 450 °C): near-identical training rows tempered at 450 °C gave **1380 MPa / 15%** (400 °C → 1340/13, 550 °C → 1090/15) → strength anchor ~1300–1380/14.

**3. Check joint coverage.** Estimated set: (280, 58), (375, 53), (~680, 30), (~900, 23), (~1350, 14) — mutually non-dominated and evenly spread across the whole frontier from the ductile austenitic corner through the γ′ knee to the tempered-martensite strength extreme, maximizing dominated hypervolume.

Final: c018, c051, c012, c056, c053
